reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports in-situ SiC formation and mechanical strengthening in a different HEA system (FeCrNiCu), but provides no data on caloric effects, order-disorder transitions, or the specific (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy. The key premises about preserving caloric performance and inertness to the phase transition are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: In-situ SiC nanoparticles can be formed in a high-entropy alloy matrix by adding Si and C during vacuum induction melting
SiC reinforcement provides dispersion strengthening and crack-bridging, improving mechanical integrity
SiC particles are inert with respect to the order-disorder transition responsible for the caloric effect
A low volume fraction (<10%) of SiC will not significantly disturb the caloric phase transition
The processing method and reinforcement effects observed in FeCrNiCu HEA are transferable to (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38
